summary: A concise introduction to khon, Thailand’s masked dance drama, in the historic Sala Chalermkrung Royal Theatre. The current visitor programme tells a Hanuman story with live traditional music, narration and English and Chinese subtitles; December 2026 dates should be checked before building a day around it.
whyGo: See an important Thai performing art in a theatre closely associated with its presentation to visitors.
The short format, subtitles and live music make the performance approachable even if you do not know the Ramakien story.
It can fit around a Grand Palace visit, and the theatre-only ticket is available separately.
bestFor: Travellers interested in Thai dance, costume, music and mythology.
Visitors who want a compact cultural performance near Bangkok’s Old Town sights.
Families or first-time viewers who appreciate a narrated story and subtitles.
skipIf: You are in Bangkok only on a weekend; the currently published visitor series runs Monday to Friday.
You need a confirmed December 2026 date before making other plans; the official calendar reviewed showed October 2026 only.
You need detailed wheelchair or step-free access information before committing; this was not published in the sources reviewed.
duration: The theatre and Grand Palace pages list each performance at 25 minutes. Allow about 1–2 hours including arrival, ticket checks and the trip from nearby Old Town sights; this is a planning estimate.
cost: The theatre-only ticket is currently listed at ฿400 per person on the Grand Palace site. The Grand Palace separately lists its ฿500 admission ticket as including the performance; verify current terms and prices before purchase, as these may change before December 2026.
hours: Current public visitor information lists three shows Monday to Friday at 13:00, 14:30 and 16:00. This is the present schedule, not a confirmed December 2026 calendar. The theatre’s published office hours are 09:00–18:00 daily.
bestTime: Choose a weekday show that fits your Old Town itinerary. The 13:00 or 14:30 slot may be easiest to pair with a morning Grand Palace visit, but allow time to exit the palace and reach the shuttle pickup. Confirm the chosen performance before travel.
gettingThere: Address: 66 Charoen Krung Road, Wang Burapha Phirom, Phra Nakhon. The theatre’s travel page lists MRT Sam Yot as the nearest metro station, with bus connections, and multiple local bus routes. Grand Palace ticket holders can use the one-way shuttle from Phiman Deves Gate, which leaves 30 minutes before each listed performance. Check the theatre map and current transit route on the day.
booking: The theatre describes weekday performances as continuing through the year and sells tickets via its ticket page / ThaiTicketMajor. Grand Palace visitors can buy a ticket package at the palace ticket counter; the show ticket is valid for seven days from purchase according to the theatre. For a standalone show, the Grand Palace site says tickets are sold at the theatre. Contact the venue to confirm December dates, English-language booking options and availability before setting plans.
accessibility: The pages reviewed do not detail step-free access, wheelchair seating, accessible toilets or hearing support. English and Chinese subtitles are provided during the show. Contact the theatre at +66 2 224 4499 or its listed office numbers to discuss mobility needs before booking.
practicalTips: The show presents an episode centered on Hanuman from the Ramakien; a short story introduction beforehand will help you follow the characters.
If visiting the Grand Palace first, use the Phiman Deves Gate shuttle and check its departure time against your ticketed show.
The official calendar reviewed was displaying October 2026, so recheck the theatre calendar or call before choosing a December weekday.
Ask before taking photographs or recording; no current audience photography policy was confirmed in the sources reviewed.
decemberNotes: December is a busy travel month, but no specific December 2026 programme, holiday closures or extra performances were confirmed in the official material reviewed. The currently published pattern is weekday performances at 13:00, 14:30 and 16:00; Thai public holidays or special events may alter it. Check the official calendar shortly before your visit and leave a buffer after the Grand Palace for the shuttle and theatre arrival.
uncertainties: The official calendar reviewed showed October 2026, not December; December performance dates and any holiday changes remain unconfirmed.
The current ฿400 theatre-only fare and the Grand Palace ticket inclusion may change before December 2026.
Accessibility details and audience photography rules were not available in the reviewed sources.
The theatre site has differing published office hours across pages; these are not showtimes.
